lessons.title: I think that…

sentences.english: I think it's very expensive.

sentences.target: Pienso que el café está rico.
sentences.english: I think the coffee is tasty.

sentences.target: Me parece que hoy hace frío.
sentences.english: It seems to me it's cold today.

sentences.target: En mi opinión, la pizza está muy rica.
sentences.english: In my opinion, the pizza is very good.
For me, it's important.

sentences.target: No estoy de acuerdo, es barato.
sentences.english: I disagree, it's cheap.

fills.english: In my opinion, it's very expensive.

lines.target: La pizza está muy rica aquí. ¿Qué opinas?
lines.english: The pizza is very good here. What do you think?

replyOptions: Creo que sí, está muy rica.

lessons.tip: creo que / pienso que / me parece que + a normal verb, no fancy grammar: creo que es caro, pienso que está rico. Say tienes razón to agree, no estoy de acuerdo to push back.

lessons.title: Because & so

example.english: I'm not going because I'm tired.

sentences.target: Tengo hambre, por eso quiero comer.
sentences.english: I'm hungry, that's why I want to eat.

sentences.target: Quiero ir, pero no tengo tiempo.
sentences.english: I want to go, but I don't have time.
Coffee or tea?

sentences.target: Es tarde, así que voy a casa.
sentences.english: It's late, so I'm going home.
Even though it's raining, I'm going to the park.

sentences.target: La casa es grande y además es barata.
sentences.english: The house is big and it's also cheap.

fills.english: I'm tired because I work a lot.
I want to go, but I can't.

lines.target: ¿Por qué no vienes a la fiesta?
lines.english: Why aren't you coming to the party?

lessons.tip: porque (one word) answers ¿por qué? (two words, a question). por eso = that's why. Chain ideas with pero, así que, aunque and you sound twice as fluent.

lessons.title: Good, bad & in between

sentences.english: The movie is very good.

sentences.target: El café es malo, pero barato.
sentences.english: The coffee is bad, but cheap.
It's better to go by metro.
This series is interesting.

sentences.target: El libro es aburrido, pero el final es increíble.
sentences.english: The book is boring, but the ending is incredible.
Everything is perfect, it's great.

lines.target: ¿Qué tal la serie nueva? ¿Es buena o mala?
lines.english: How's the new series? Is it good or bad?

replyOptions: Creo que es genial, la quiero ver otra vez.

lessons.tip: Opinions with es + adjective: es interesante, es increíble. Many are twins of English (terrible, normal, perfecto). Adjectives agree with the noun (la película es buena), but genial never changes.

lessons.title: Comparing

example.target: Es tan caro como el otro.
example.english: It's as expensive as the other one.

items.english: I don't care / it's all the same to me

sentences.target: El metro es más fácil que el autobús.
sentences.english: The metro is easier than the bus.

sentences.target: Este hotel es menos caro que el otro.
sentences.english: This hotel is less expensive than the other one.

sentences.target: Mi hermano es mejor que yo.
sentences.english: My brother is better than me.

sentences.target: La pizza es tan buena como la pasta.
sentences.english: The pizza is as good as the pasta.

sentences.target: Es el mejor restaurante de la ciudad.
sentences.english: It's the best restaurant in the city.

sentences.target: Tu amigo me cae bien, es muy simpático.
sentences.english: I like your friend, he's very nice.

fills.english: The car is bigger than the motorcycle.
The weather is worse today than yesterday.
My house is as big as yours.

lines.target: ¿Vamos al bar de siempre o al nuevo?
lines.english: Shall we go to the usual bar or the new one?

lessons.tip: más/menos + adjective + que: más caro que, menos grande que. tan + adjective + como = as … as. The odd ones: mejor que / peor que (never más bueno).

lessons.title: Natural fillers

sentences.english: Well, I don't know, let's see.
It's just that I have a lot of work.
Honestly, I don't feel like it.
I missed the train, oh well.
I might be late.

sentences.target: Me gusta el café, sobre todo por la mañana.
sentences.english: I like coffee, especially in the morning.

fills.english: It's just that I'm very tired.

lines.target: Mañana tengo un examen y no estudié nada.
lines.english: Tomorrow I have an exam and I didn't study at all.

lessons.tip: Fillers buy thinking time: pues, o sea, a ver, es que. Natives say them every sentence. a lo mejor + normal verb = maybe: a lo mejor llego tarde.

lessons.title: Suggesting

items.english: What do you think of that?

example.english: How about we go to the cinema?

sentences.english: How about we go to the cinema?
What if we go to the park tomorrow?
Where shall we meet? At your place?

sentences.target: Nos vemos allí a las ocho.
sentences.english: See you there at eight.
Shall I bring something? I have wine.

sentences.target: ¿Cuándo puedes? Yo estoy libre el sábado.
sentences.english: When can you? I'm free on Saturday.

fills.english: How about we go to the cinema?

lines.target: ¿Qué tal si vamos al cine el sábado?
lines.english: How about we go to the cinema on Saturday?

replyOptions: Perfecto, ¿a qué hora te viene bien?

lessons.tip: ¿Qué tal si…? / ¿Y si…? + a normal verb = how about…? ¿Qué tal si vamos al cine? ¿Y si vamos mañana? Zero grammar, just a frame to fill.

lessons.title: Going out

sentences.target: Esta noche vamos a un bar.
sentences.english: Tonight we're going to a bar.
The concert is on Saturday.
Shall we have dinner on the terrace? It's warm.

sentences.target: Quiero una botana con la cerveza.
sentences.english: I want a snack with the beer.
sentences.spain: Quiero un pincho con la cerveza.

sentences.english: Do you want a drink?
I'll buy the first round.

fills.english: Today there's a concert in the park.

fills.after: es a las nueve de la noche.
fills.english: Dinner is at nine at night.

lines.target: ¿Qué hacemos esta noche?
lines.english: What are we doing tonight?

replyOptions: ¿Qué tal si vamos a un bar?

lessons.tip: la comida = the main meal of the day (lunch in Spain and much of Latin America, but also just 'food'); la cena = dinner. Spain says la copa and el pincho where Mexico says el trago and la botana.

lessons.title: Meeting new people

example.english: Let me introduce you to my friend.

items.english: Do you want something to drink?

sentences.target: Ana, te presento a mi amigo Luis.
sentences.english: Ana, let me introduce you to my friend Luis.
Nice to meet you. – Likewise.
Do we know each other? I think so.

sentences.target: ¿De qué conoces a Pedro? –Es mi compañero.
sentences.english: How do you know Pedro? – He's my colleague.

sentences.target: Bienvenido a mi casa. Pasa y ponte cómodo.
sentences.english: Welcome to my home. Come in and make yourself comfortable.
Thanks for inviting me. – You're welcome.

fills.english: Let me introduce you to my sister.
Do you want something to drink?

lines.target: Te presento a mi hermana Sara.
lines.english: Let me introduce you to my sister Sara.

lessons.tip: te presento a… = let me introduce you to… (the a stays). Reply with mucho gusto / igualmente (same to you). bienvenido becomes bienvenida for a woman.

lessons.title: Running late

example.target: Lo siento, no voy a poder.
example.english: Sorry, I won't be able to.

items.english: I'll be there in five minutes

sentences.target: Hay mucho tráfico, llego en cinco minutos.
sentences.english: There's a lot of traffic, I'll be there in five minutes.
I'm almost there, one moment.

sentences.target: Lo siento, no voy a poder ir hoy.
sentences.english: Sorry, I won't be able to go today.
The concert got cancelled.

sentences.target: Me quedé dormido, estoy en camino.
sentences.english: I overslept, I'm on my way.

sentences.target: Se me complicó el trabajo, mejor mañana.
sentences.english: Work got complicated, better tomorrow.

fills.english: I won't be able to go.
There's a lot of traffic today.

lines.target: ¿Dónde estás? Ya son las nueve.
lines.english: Where are you? It's already nine.

replyOptions: Estoy en camino, llego en cinco minutos.

lessons.tip: ya + chunk = on my way: ya voy llegando, ya casi llego. Gender shows in feelings and states: me quedé dormido (man) / me quedé dormida (woman).

lessons.title: Splitting the bill

items.english: How many of you will there be?

sentences.english: Are you all coming?
There are five of us, and you?

sentences.target: Yo invito, tú pagas la próxima vez.
sentences.english: I'll pay, you pay next time.
Let's go halves, OK?
You owe me ten euros.
We're all going together, anyone else?

lines.target: La cuenta, por favor. ¿Cómo pagamos?
lines.english: The bill, please. How do we pay?

lessons.tip: In Latin America you say ustedes to a group; Spain says vosotros (¿Vosotros venís?). You only need to recognise vosotros, but you will hear it all over Spain: venís, tenéis, vais.

lessons.title: Phone calls

sentences.english: I have an important call.

sentences.target: No contesto porque no tengo señal.
sentences.english: I'm not answering because I have no signal.

sentences.target: Estoy sin batería, necesito el cargador.
sentences.english: I'm out of battery, I need the charger.
I have no credit to call.

sentences.target: Tengo tu contacto en el celular.
sentences.english: I have your contact on my phone.
sentences.spain: Tengo tu contacto en el móvil.

sentences.english: Do you want to do a video call?

fills.english: My phone is out of battery.
I want to answer the call.

lines.target: ¿Por qué no contestas el celular?
lines.english: Why don't you answer your phone?

lessons.tip: Many phone words are cognates or English imports: la aplicación, la videollamada, el audio. Nouns ending in -ción are feminine (la aplicación), -o is usually masculine (el audio, el contacto).

lessons.title: Picking up

items.english: I can't hear / it's not audible

sentences.english: Hello? Who's speaking?
Hi, is Ana there? – Yes, speaking.
I can't hear anything, can you hear me?

sentences.target: Se cortó la llamada, te llamo luego.
sentences.english: The call cut out, I'll call you later.
Call me tomorrow, please.
Call me back, we'll talk soon.

lines.target: ¿Aló? ¿Está Ana?
lines.english: Hello? Is Ana there?

lessons.tip: Phones are answered differently by country: ¿Bueno? (Mexico), ¿Aló? (Andes, Caribbean), ¿Diga? / ¿Dígame? (Spain). Llámame and devuélveme glue a pronoun onto the verb: call me, give it back to me.

lessons.title: Text shortcuts

sentences.english: Haha, how good!
Love you lots, see you tomorrow.
Thanks for the message.
Where are you? Please call me.

sentences.target: Yo tb voy, xq quiero verte.
sentences.english: I'm going too, because I want to see you.
Kisses, we'll talk tomorrow.

lines.target: Grax por la ayuda 🙏
lines.english: Thanks for the help 🙏

lessons.tip: Texting squeezes sounds: q = que, xq = porque, tb = también, mñn = mañana, tqm = te quiero mucho, ntp = no te preocupes. Spain also uses tkm and k for que. They are for friends, never for your boss.

lessons.title: Chat verbs

sentences.english: Send me a message, please.
Answer me when you can.

sentences.target: Voy a reenviar la foto al grupo de WhatsApp.
sentences.english: I'm going to forward the photo to the WhatsApp group.
I deleted the chat.

sentences.target: Te mando una nota de voz.
sentences.english: I'll send you a voice note.
Why do you leave me on read?

lines.target: Te mandé un mensaje y no me respondes.
lines.english: I sent you a message and you don't reply.

replyOptions: Perdón, estoy ocupado, te respondo luego.

lessons.tip: Chat commands are imperatives with the pronoun glued on: mándame (send me), respóndeme (answer me), avísame (let me know). The written accent keeps the stress in the same place.

lessons.title: Social media

sentences.english: I'm uploading a photo to my profile.
I love your post.
Will you tag me in the photo?
I want to share this video.
I have lots of new followers.

sentences.target: No me gusta ese comentario, lo bloqueo.
sentences.english: I don't like that comment, I'm blocking it.

fills.english: I'm going to watch a new video.
I put a filter on the photo.

lines.target: Subí una foto nueva, ¿la viste?
lines.english: I uploaded a new photo, did you see it?

lessons.tip: Social media vocabulary is half English: el hashtag, el like, el filtro, el perfil. Spanish verbs do the work: subir una foto, etiquetar, compartir, bloquear. Spain writes vídeo with an accent.

lessons.title: How I feel

sentences.english: I'm happy because it's Friday.

sentences.target: Estoy triste, no tengo ganas de salir.
sentences.english: I'm sad, I don't feel like going out.
I'm angry because I arrived late.

sentences.target: Estoy nervioso, tengo un examen mañana.
sentences.english: I'm nervous, I have an exam tomorrow.
I'm excited, I'm going to travel.
I'm fed up with work.

lines.target: ¿Cómo estás hoy?
lines.english: How are you today?

lessons.tip: estoy + adjective = a mood that changes: estoy feliz, estoy nervioso. The ending matches who speaks: a woman says estoy nerviosa, estoy cansada. Spain says enfadado where Latin America says enojado.

lessons.title: Feeling nouns

sentences.target: Hay mucha alegría en mi casa.
sentences.english: There's a lot of joy in my house.
I'm afraid of the exam.

sentences.target: La risa de mi hermana es genial.
sentences.english: My sister's laugh is great.

sentences.target: Es una sorpresa para mi mamá.
sentences.english: It's a surprise for my mom.
Anger doesn't help.

sentences.target: Tengo nervios, es mi primer día de trabajo.
sentences.english: I'm nervous, it's my first day at work.

fills.english: There's a lot of joy here.

lines.target: Mañana es mi primer día de trabajo y tengo muchos nervios.
lines.english: Tomorrow is my first day at work and I'm very nervous.

replyOptions: Creo que todo va a salir bien.

lessons.tip: Feelings as nouns end in -dad / -ción / -za / -o: la tristeza, la sorpresa, el miedo. Use tener for some: tengo miedo, tengo nervios. los nervios and las lágrimas are always plural. Spain says el enfado for el enojo.

lessons.title: Reactions

items.english: Cheer up! / You can do it!

sentences.english: I have a new job. – Great!
I lost my phone. – Oh no!

sentences.target: Me quedé dormido en la reunión. –¡Qué vergüenza!
sentences.english: I fell asleep in the meeting. – How embarrassing!
I almost arrived late. – What a scare!
I've done the exam. – What a relief!
It's my birthday. – Congratulations!

lines.target: Perdí mi cartera y no tengo dinero.
lines.english: I lost my wallet and I have no money.

lessons.tip: ¡Qué + noun/adjective! is the all-purpose reaction: ¡Qué susto!, ¡Qué suerte!, ¡Qué bien! No verb needed. The accent matters: qué (what/how) vs que (that).

lessons.title: Being there for someone

items.spain: echo de menos a mi familia

sentences.english: How are you feeling today?
Tell me, I'm here for you.

sentences.target: No te preocupes, todo va a estar bien.
sentences.english: Don't worry, everything will be OK.
I need to talk, do you have time?
I miss my family.
sentences.spain: Echo de menos a mi familia.

sentences.english: I miss you a lot, come here.
sentences.spain: Te echo mucho de menos, ven aquí.

fills.english: Everything is going to be OK.

lines.target: ¿Qué te pasa? Hoy estás muy triste.
lines.english: What's wrong? You're very sad today.

replyOptions: Extraño a mi familia, necesito hablar.

lessons.tip: te extraño = I miss you (Spain: te echo de menos). no te preocupes uses the tú command: negative commands borrow the present tense (no te preocupes, no llores). Short, warm chunks beat perfect grammar here.

lessons.title: Personality

sentences.english: My brother is very quiet.

sentences.target: Mi amiga es habladora, habla mucho.
sentences.english: My friend is talkative, she talks a lot.

sentences.target: Mi jefe es trabajador y generoso.
sentences.english: My boss is hard-working and generous.

sentences.target: Mi primo es flojo, duerme mucho.
sentences.english: My cousin is lazy, he sleeps a lot.
sentences.spain: Mi primo es vago, duerme mucho.

sentences.target: No me cae bien, es muy grosero.
sentences.english: I don't like him, he's very rude.

sentences.target: Mi mamá es muy paciente y valiente.
sentences.english: My mom is very patient and brave.

lines.target: ¿Cómo es tu jefe?
lines.english: What's your boss like?

lessons.tip: Personality words: -oso/-osa (celoso, curioso), -or/-ora (trabajador, hablador). They agree with the person: mi hermana es habladora, mi hermano es hablador. Spain says vago for flojo.

lessons.title: What's up?

items.english: What have you been up to?

items.target: hace mucho que no te veo
items.english: I haven't seen you in ages

sentences.english: What's up? How's everything?
Nothing new, getting by.
Long time no see! So good to see you!
All good, and how about you?

sentences.target: Hace mucho que no te veo, ¿qué has hecho?
sentences.english: I haven't seen you in ages, what have you been up to?
What's new? – Nothing, working a lot.

fills.english: I haven't seen you in ages.

lines.target: ¡Hola! ¡Cuánto tiempo! ¿Qué onda?
lines.english: Hi! Long time no see! What's up?

lessons.tip: Every region opens a chat differently: ¿Qué onda? (Mexico), ¿Qué hay? / ¿Qué pasa? (Spain), ¿Qué más? (Colombia). All mean what's up. ¿Y tú qué tal? bounces the question back, and nada nuevo is the lazy honest answer.

lessons.title: When I was a kid

items.english: I went / I used to go
it was (weather) / I used to do

sentences.target: Cuando era niño, vivía en un pueblo.
sentences.english: When I was a kid, I lived in a town.

sentences.target: De niño, tenía una bicicleta roja.
sentences.english: As a kid, I had a red bike.

sentences.target: Todos los veranos iba a la playa con mi familia.
sentences.english: Every summer I went to the beach with my family.

sentences.target: En esa época no tenía celular.
sentences.english: Back then I didn't have a cell phone.
sentences.spain: En esa época no tenía móvil.

sentences.target: Cuando era niño, en verano hacía mucho calor.
sentences.english: When I was a kid, it was very hot in summer.

sentences.target: Solía jugar al fútbol con mis primos.
sentences.english: I used to play football with my cousins.

fills.english: When I was a kid, I lived here.
As a kid I had a bike.
Every summer I went to the beach.
I used to live in a small house.

lines.target: ¿Dónde vivías de niño?
lines.english: Where did you live as a kid?

lessons.tip: The imperfecto describes how things used to be: era (I was), tenía (I had), vivía (I lived), iba (I went), hacía (it was, weather). Memorise them as chunks: cuando era niño…, de niño tenía…

lessons.title: Where I live & work

items.english: What do you do for work?

sentences.english: Are you from here? – No, I'm new here.

sentences.target: Vine por trabajo, me mudé hace dos días.
sentences.english: I came for work, I moved two days ago.
I live in a quiet neighbourhood.

sentences.target: ¿En qué trabajas? –Trabajo en una empresa grande.
sentences.english: What do you do? – I work at a big company.

sentences.target: Mi horario es de nueve a cinco.
sentences.english: My schedule is from nine to five.

sentences.target: Estudio en la universidad, mi carrera es difícil.
sentences.english: I study at the university, my degree is hard.

fills.english: What do you do for work?

lines.target: ¿Eres de aquí?
lines.english: Are you from here?

replyOptions: No, soy nuevo aquí. Vine por trabajo.

lessons.tip: trabajo en + place, estudio en + place, no article needed: trabajo en una empresa, estudio en la universidad. me mudé = I moved (to a new home).

lessons.title: Compliments & manners

items.english: Hope it goes well for you!

sentences.english: You look great today.
What a pretty dress!
Good job, Ana!
Excuse me, may I come in?
Thanks a lot. – My pleasure.
Sorry, can you help me? – No problem.

fills.english: Hope it goes well for you!
Excuse me, may I come in?

lines.target: Mañana voy de viaje a la playa.
lines.english: Tomorrow I'm going on a trip to the beach.

lessons.tip: ¡Que + wish! as a chunk: ¡Que te vaya bien!, ¡Que lo pases bien! = may it go well for you. Don't analyse the grammar, just say it. Politeness tools: con permiso, disculpa, con gusto, sin problema.

lessons.title: Goodbyes

sentences.english: See you soon! Bye!
It's late, get some rest!

sentences.target: ¡Buen fin de semana! Nos vemos el lunes.
sentences.english: Have a good weekend! See you Monday.
Say hi to your family.

sentences.target: Dale mis saludos a tu mamá.
sentences.english: Give my regards to your mom.
A hug, we'll talk.

lines.target: Ya es tarde, me voy a casa. ¡Cuídate mucho!
lines.english: It's late, I'm going home. Take good care!

lessons.tip: Goodbyes are wishes too: ¡Que descanses! (may you rest), ¡Que tengas buen día! Don't analyse them, just copy them. ¡Chao! works everywhere, and un abrazo ends a friendly message.
